text: Affected mart columns if gold.fx_rate.conversion_rate is wrong (value or influence, directly or via intermediates): mart.fact_po_line.savings_amt (direct, derived); mart.po_supplier_summary.total_savings (aggregated); mart.supplier_spend.total_savings (aggregated, plus identity via po_supplier_summary); mart.shipment_fact.ext_amount_usd and gross_margin_usd (via pg_temp.stg_ship, derived then identity); mart.customer_snapshot.lifetime_revenue (aggregated, via shipment_fact and pg_temp.cust_metrics.revenue); mart.customer_snapshot.segment (conditional value from pg_temp.cust_metrics.segment_hint, which is influenced by shipment_fact.ext_amount_usd). Filter edges onto mart tables are excluded as not value/influence. Boundaries/refusals were not checked with gaps.

Dropping s2p.po_distribution.amount_cancelled would affect 9 mart columns across 3 tables.

mart.fact_po_line (direct, value, conditional): line_amt, savings_amt, should_cost.

mart.po_supplier_summary (indirect):
- total_spend: value, aggregated, from fact_po_line.line_amt.
- total_savings: value, aggregated, from fact_po_line.savings_amt.
- spend_rank: influence, from fact_po_line.line_amt.

mart.supplier_spend (indirect):
- total_spend: value, aggregated, from fact_po_line.line_amt. It also gets a value from po_supplier_summary.total_spend.
- total_savings: value, aggregated, from fact_po_line.savings_amt. It also gets a value from po_supplier_summary.total_savings.
- spend_rank: influence from fact_po_line.line_amt. It also gets a value from po_supplier_summary.spend_rank.

The column also filters rows of mart.fact_po_line (edge a1d66c2b125fbae6a8cba436). That is a filter, not a value or influence, so I left it out of the list.

Other places it feeds are not mart columns: the ad-hoc result columns of medium/m1_procurement_savings.sql and the result of h2_po_fact_load.sql line 436. No boundaries or refusals were found on this lineage.

mart.po_supplier_summary.total_spend is fed (aggregated, pre-aggregation) by mart.fact_po_line.line_amt (edge bdfa0cdbea618eeb3f02b1f8, h2_po_fact_load.sql:345). line_amt is fed (conditional, h2_po_fact_load.sql:31) by six columns that nothing feeds, so they are the ultimate sources: s2p.po_distribution.amount_cancelled, s2p.po_distribution.amount_ordered, s2p.po_distribution.quantity_cancelled, s2p.po_distribution.quantity_ordered, s2p.po_line.matching_basis, s2p.po_line_location.price_override. No boundaries or refusals on this lineage. Filter and influence edges were excluded (value flow only).

Filtering columns along the value lineage of mart.po_supplier_summary.total_spend (all pre-aggregation):

On mart.po_supplier_summary (load at line 345): mart.fact_po_line.status_code.

On mart.fact_po_line (the table feeding line_amt; loads at lines 31, 375 and 408):
- gold.dim_status: datasource_num_id, status_code
- mart.fact_po_line: line_amt, status_code
- s2p.po_distribution: amount_cancelled, amount_ordered, distribution_id, last_modification_date_time, quantity_cancelled, quantity_ordered
- s2p.po_header: document_status, last_modification_date_time, po_header_id
- s2p.po_line: line_status, matching_basis
- s2p.po_line_location: last_modification_date_time, line_location_id, price_override
- s2p.req_distribution: distribution_quantity, last_modification_date_time, req_distribution_id
- s2p.req_header: approved_date

No boundaries or refusals limit this.

Yes. The graph shows no boundaries or refusals on mart.shipment_fact.gross_margin_usd or on its intermediate pg_temp.stg_ship.gross_margin_usd, so it is fully traceable.

Path: the column is loaded from pg_temp.stg_ship.gross_margin_usd by two statements (h4_nightly_load.sql:106 and :121), both as identity value flows. The staging column is built at h4_nightly_load.sql:40.

Ultimate source columns (value flow only):
- lgx.shipment_line.shipped_qty (derived)
- lgx.shipment_line.unit_selling_price (derived)
- lgx.item_master.std_cost (derived)
- gold.fx_rate.conversion_rate (derived)
- gold.fx_rate.to_ccy (conditional)

I left out filters and influences (for example gold.fx_rate.from_ccy, rate_date and loaded_at, which only influence the staging column) because you asked for value flow only.
